At Ashdown we are Caring, Curious, Confident.
Welcome to Ashdown Primary School
Thank you for visiting our website.
We hope it gives you a glimpse into the many wonderful things happening at our creative, nurturing, and ambitious school.
At Ashdown, we are proud to offer a vibrant learning environment where every child is supported to thrive academically, socially, and emotionally. I feel privileged and honoured to lead such an inspiring school community.
At Ashdown, we value everyone, nurture their strengths and enable them to flourish.
The Designated Safeguarding Leads for the school are Dawn Gibbs, Debbie Stephen, Barrie Lucas, Lisa Birchard, Helen Warner and Joe Reardon. If you have any worries or concerns please email them using the email address: safeguarding@ashdown.e-sussex.sch.uk. All information is treated as confidential following our school's safeguarding policy

Life Choices and Careers Related Learning
At Ashdown, Life Choices and Careers Related Learning is thoughtfully embedded across the curriculum. We help children develop an early awareness of the opportunities available to them, inspiring them to think about the choices they can make now and in the future.
Whether it's learning about the role of scientists in science lessons, or discussing hopes and dreams during PSHE&C, children are encouraged to explore different careers and life paths. Visits, visitors, and real-world examples help bring these opportunities to life, as we explore the roles and journeys of the people we meet.
Throughout the year, we focus on Six Key Skills: Resilience, Communication, Respect, Teamwork, Independence, and Staying Positive. These skills are closely linked to our school values and Golden Rules, helping children grow in confidence and preparing them for lifelong learning.
Which of our focus skills do you think these jobs require?
Chef Scientist Shop Assistant Builder Doctor Journalist
What can you do to support your child?
We believe that real-life stories and experiences bring learning to life. Whether you have a salaried job, run your own business, volunteer, or care for others, your experiences are valuable. Talking to your child about what you do, where you go, and the steps you took to get there — including important life decisions — can help them understand the many different paths people take in life.
Do you have a passion for helping children build the skills they need for the future? Do you think it’s important to prepare them now for the choices and opportunities ahead?
If so, we would love for you to get involved! Sharing your career or life journey with the children — especially in connection with our focus skills of Resilience, Communication, Respect, Teamwork, Independence, and Staying Positive — can make a real difference. Please speak to your child’s teacher to find out how you can help support Life Choices and Careers Learning, and even contribute to other areas of the wider curriculum.

Peer Mediators
Children in Year 5 have the opportunity to become Peer Mediators. Their job is to help resolve minor playground conflicts through restorative conversations, ensuring everyone feels heard and respected. They listen, remain neutral and guide peers toward a solution that everyone is happy with. Easily identifiable by their purple lanyards, they promote our school values of respect, resilience, opportunity, support and trust. By fostering a positive and peaceful environment, our Peer Mediators play an important role in making our school a supportive, caring a peaceful place.

Science ambassadors
At Ashdown Primary School we believe the teaching and learning of science is key to understanding the world around us and to help prepare our children for the future.
Each year group has two science ambassadors They are issued with an official lab coat, which they wear with pride!
Their duties include:
- to clearly explain what they have been learning in science each term using scientific vocabulary. This will be shared in termly meetings through use of their science books.
- to help with the organisation of science resources
-to monitor their class science ruck sack
- to assist teachers in setting up their classroom for science lessons
- to assist visitors around the school and discuss science at Ashdown Primary
- to feedback the thoughts and opinions of their class to science leaders/teachers
-to try out new science equipment
